nodes.label: SWIG-Generated Python Wrapper
nodes.rationale: PyChrono is a set of SWIG-generated Python modules that correspond one-to-one to Chrono units; SWIG's limitations (no templates, no nested classes) drive most of the documented Python/C++ divergences.

nodes.label: Template Specialization Naming Convention
nodes.rationale: Python has no templates, so every templated C++ class is wrapped as its most relevant specializations under the C++ alias names (ChVector3d, ChMatrixDynamicd, ChFramed); std::vector containers get a vector_ prefix (chrono.vector_ChVector3d) to keep the mapping predictable.

nodes.label: ChVector x/y/z Member Mapping
nodes.rationale: C++ accessors x()/y()/z() return references; the parentheses were dropped and mapped to direct data members in Python to avoid reference-semantics issues. The same treatment applies to quaternion components e0..e3.

nodes.label: Automatic Shared Pointer Handling
nodes.rationale: C++ shared pointers are template-based and templates are unsupported in Python, but this is not an issue because PyChrono handles shared-pointer objects automatically: constructing the Python object also constructs the referenced object.

nodes.label: Manual Downcasting via CastToXXX
nodes.rationale: Upcasting works automatically (including for shared pointers), but a function returning a base-class pointer cannot convey the derived type to Python. Automatic downcasting exists only for ChFunction and ChAsset descendants; everything else needs CastToXXX() helpers, analogous to C++ dynamic_cast.

nodes.label: Nested Class Flattening
nodes.rationale: SWIG does not support nested classes in Python; they can only be ignored or flattened. PyChrono flattens every nested class into the upper namespace (ChContactContainer::ReportContactCallback becomes chrono.ReportContactCallback, VisualizationType::MESH becomes VisualizationType_MESH).

nodes.label: Python Object Creation and Lifetime
nodes.rationale: C++ offers stack and heap creation with manual delete; Python has one construction form and automatic lifetime management. A consequence users must internalize is that '=' assigns a handle rather than copying, so two names can refer to one ChSystem.

nodes.label: Unmapped C++ Classes Diagnostic
nodes.rationale: A mapped return value echoes as a pychrono type proxying a Swig Object; an unmapped one echoes only as a bare Swig Object pointer that is unusable in Python. This echo difference is the documented way to detect coverage gaps.
